correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier cardinal identity gives every quadrature weight by substitution; sign comparison uses the explicit alternating Dirichlet sine quotient and circular distances. The row Gram matrix of a unitary Fourier matrix after only one row is replaced reduces to one 2-by-2 block, yielding all singular values. Two small-angle limits prove the joint collision law. The positive finite-domain determinant and delta=0, delta=1/2 boundaries were checked. The standalone checker passed 1896 finite numerical assertions; those do not replace the all-integer analytic proof.

value.rationale: A natural single-sensor drift benchmark for exactly integrating the full trigonometric band yields an all-odd-size positivity classification, a unique sign-changing neighbor, exact optimal bounded-noise norm, entire singular spectrum, and a joint critical N^-1 collision law. It draws a meaningful distinction between stable quadrature and unstable Fourier coefficient inversion and contrasts with the published symmetric two-node collision phenomenon. These are an exact motivated phase diagram, not a normalization-only observation; they do not claim a general multi-node theorem.
